cacheKey.normalizedQuery: RATCHET_ANCHOR_REF is hardcoded to the single literal main with no fallback (e.g. origin/main). Verified: git -C repoRoot ls-tree --name-only main scripts/ correctly fails closed (exit 1, RATCHET ANCHOR UNRESOLVABLE, not a silent skip) when git itself is unreachable (tested via PATH stripped of git). But in a shallow or single-branch CI checkout that never creates a local main ref (e.g. git clone --depth=1 --branch=story/B-dc83), this same fail-closed path would trip and both the wired default gate detection AND --baseline-shrink-proof would go red even though nothing is actually broken -- a spurious failure, not a caught defect. This repo has no .github/workflows today so the risk is currently latent, not an active break, and fail-closed is the safer failure direction (never silently passes), so this is advisory rather than blocking. Worth a one-line code comment or CI checkout note (fetch-depth: 0 / ensure a local main ref exists) so a future CI adopter does not spend time debugging a spurious red gate. Fixed as the reviewer specified: the anchor now resolves against an ORDERED CANDIDATE LIST (RATCHET_ANCHOR_REFS = [main, origin/main]) instead of the single literal main. REPRODUCED THE SPURIOUS RED FIRST, on a real repo rather than by argument: git clone --no-local --depth=1 --branch=story/B-dc83 produced a checkout with NO local main, and the pre-fix script there failed with RATCHET ANCHOR UNRESOLVABLE ... Not a valid object name main even though nothing was broken. After fetching the trunk as a remote-tracking ref only (origin/main present, local main still absent) the FIXED script in that same clone PASSES: ratchet: all 17 tolerated orphans exist in scripts/ on origin/main, anchor: resolved origin/main (first match of main, origin/main). DESIGN, chosen so the fallback cannot become a weakening: readAnchorScriptsForRef reads ONE ref; readAnchorScripts walks the candidates and RETURNS ON FIRST SUCCESS, so tolerance always comes from exactly ONE tree. The trees are never unioned (unioning would let a name absent from main but present in a stale origin/main become tolerable) and origin/main is never even read when local main resolves, so it cannot be shopped for extra permissiveness. Both candidates remain out-of-file git history, so nothing about the in-file-vs-out-of-file root cause changes. A header note warns that adding a NON-trunk candidate (HEAD, the story branch) WOULD be a real weakening. FAIL-CLOSED PRESERVED AND PROVEN in three directions: all candidates deleted from the clone -> exit 1 naming both, no anchor candidate resolved (tried 2): main -> ... ; origin/main -> ...; git itself unreachable (PATH stripped) -> exit 1 naming both with ENOENT each; and the self-test live-anchor check fails closed identically. The message names every candidate tried with its individual reason, states that an in-file fallback is exactly what F-003 rejected so none exists, and points a CI adopter at fetch-depth 0. F-003 PROPERTY PRESERVED: created scripts/verify-f007-probe.mjs and added it to BASELINE (the only in-file list) in ONE edit -> shrink-proof FAILED with BASELINE GREW ... does NOT exist in scripts/ on main and self-test FAILED via its live-BASELINE check; restored. F-001 PROPERTY PRESERVED: wired verify-dev-memory.mjs via a package.json script and dropped its single BASELINE line (17->16) -> all three modes exit 0, and diffing against the pre-shrink file shows the ENTIRE required change was one removed line, ZERO constant edits; restored. THREE new self-test cases cover multi-candidate resolution and are MUTATION-PROVEN falsifiable, not decorative: making readAnchorScripts union the trees fails the no-union case; adding an in-file BASELINE fallback on total miss fails the fail-closed case; breaking fall-through (fail on first miss, i.e. the F-007 bug itself) fails the fall-through case. Each mutant exited 1 and was reverted. Header updated to document the candidate list, first-match-wins/no-union semantics, and that fail-closed still applies when all candidates miss. validate --lint pass (tsc: 3 tsconfigs); tree clean apart from this file; lattice.config.json, packages/main/src and the DONE-required root suite untouched.

devMemory.summary: A test's generic top-level assertion failure message can mask the REAL underlying cause -- don't trust a surface error message as the root cause without tracing what actually happened first, especially when triaging a test as 'unrelated pre-existing' to justify not fixing it.
devMemory.lesson: When a test fails with a message that sounds infrastructure/environment-related ('shim fired', 'marker never created', 'injection did not run'), and you're tempted to conclude 'unrelated, pre-existing, out of scope' -- verify by tracing the ACTUAL execution path (add temporary debug logging, or read the CLI's real stdout/stderr before the fixture's own assertion wrapper summarizes it), not just by checking 'is this file in my diff'. A file being untouched by your diff does NOT mean your diff didn't break it -- a new gate/check anywhere in the shared call path the file exercises can block it before it ever reaches the logic its own assertions describe. This is the same root-cause class as F-008 (a new gate running before pre-existing code the test expects to reach), just with a MORE misleading surface symptom this time.
devMemory.reusePrompt: test failure message sounds like infrastructure/environment / tempted to call it unrelated pre-existing / spawn_task for a test failure / verify root cause before triaging as out of scope / shim fired marker never created

devMemory.summary: Rerouting a lock/path argument at a call site can be a no-op if the callee already independently re-derives the same shared root internally.
devMemory.lesson: acquireStoryTransitionLock(root, storyId) looked like it needed a stable-root reroute to survive a winning DONE deleting the worktree it was called from -- but storyTransitionLockPath already resolves root through resolveSharedLockRoot (git-common-dir based, B-d877 R2 FIX B) BEFORE touching disk, so ANY root string passed in (worktree path or main repo root) resolves to the identical shared lock directory. The reroute compiled, built, and even made the target smoke test pass -- because the REAL fix (a separate StoryArtifactMissingError translation) was landed in the same commit, masking that the reroute itself did nothing. A REVIEW reviewer caught it by comparing storyTransitionLockPath(worktreePath, id) vs storyTransitionLockPath(mainRepoRoot, id) directly and finding them identical. Before adding a 'fix' that reroutes an argument into a shared/lock/root-resolution function, read the CALLEE's own resolution logic first -- if it already normalizes via git-common-dir or similar, the caller-side reroute is redundant. When a test passes after a multi-part fix, that does not mean every part of the fix is load-bearing; isolate and re-test each part before crediting it as the actual fix.
devMemory.reusePrompt: adding a stable-root/shared-root reroute before a lock or path helper / lock directory disappears with worktree teardown / fix passes tests but reviewer says a change is a no-op / multi-part fix, unclear which part is load-bearing

devMemory.summary: lattice.config.json's validate.commands does NOT cover every test file in the repo -- the project's root npm test (full-suite-runner.js, driven by package.json's much longer test:serial-reference script list) is a broader, separate canonical test command that can catch regressions lattice validate and multiple REVIEW rounds all miss.
devMemory.lesson: lattice validate (and by extension every REVIEW round that relies on it as its evidence) only exercises whatever is explicitly listed in lattice.config.json's validate.commands array. The project's root package.json 'test' script (full-suite-runner.js) runs a much longer, separately-maintained list that is NOT a subset check against validate.commands -- a file can exist in one list, the other, both, or neither. For any change touching a widely-shared code path (state-machine guards, core registries, shared handler utilities), run the project's root npm test at least once before DONE, not just lattice validate. Also: npm test's own HEAD-drift self-protection aborts the whole run if anything commits mid-run (e.g. a concurrent dev_memory_capture/finding_resolve auto-commit) -- run it with zero concurrent git-mutating commands, or its own protective abort looks like a mass test failure when it is not.
devMemory.reusePrompt: npm test failing but lattice validate passed / REVIEW rounds missed a regression / validate.commands not comprehensive / full-suite-runner.js / full-suite identity drift HEAD changed during execution
